content.title: FOOD FACTS THAT SOUND MADE UP BUT {{ARE 100% REAL}}
facts: **Pineapple** actually eats you back — it contains bromelain, an enzyme so strong it breaks down proteins, which is why your tongue tingles after too much fresh pineapple.
**Cashews** never get sold in their shell — the shell contains a resin so caustic it's related to poison ivy, so it's removed and destroyed before cashews ever reach a store.
**Nutmeg** in large enough doses is a legitimate hallucinogen — historical sailors and prisoners have used it to get high, and just 2 whole nutmegs can cause real toxicity.
**Rhubarb** stalks are a common dessert ingredient, but its leaves contain enough oxalic acid to be genuinely poisonous if eaten in quantity.
**Carrots** were originally purple, not orange — the orange variety we eat today was selectively bred in the Netherlands centuries later.
**Cheese** can be legally aged for over a decade — some Parmigiano-Reggiano wheels are matured for 10+ years and are still perfectly safe to eat.
**Almonds** are technically not a nut at all — they're the seed found inside a fruit that looks similar to a peach.
**Chocolate** was used as currency by the Aztecs — cacao beans were valuable enough to literally buy goods and pay taxes with.
**Follow along** – for more surprising, fact-checked nutrition truths like this.
content.caption:
The pineapple fact throws people every time — bromelain doesn't just sit there, it actively digests the proteins in your mouth's soft tissue, which is why eating a lot of fresh pineapple can leave your tongue feeling raw or tingly within minutes. Cashews are wild too: the shell contains urushiol, the exact same irritant compound found in poison ivy, which is why raw cashews-in-shell are never sold to consumers and are always steamed or roasted first to neutralize it. And nutmeg sounds harmless sitting in your spice rack, but it contains myristicin, a compound your liver converts into something with amphetamine-like effects at high doses — which is exactly why more than a teaspoon or two is considered unsafe. Everyone's tolerance and body chemistry is different, so this isn't a reason to fear your spice cabinet, just to respect it.
